skill.name: iterate-pr
skill.description: Investigates pull request failures, addresses valid review feedback, applies targeted fixes, and repeats the CI cycle until required checks pass.
skill.summary: Resolve CI failures and review feedback through a structured pull request iteration workflow.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and code fences. The shell substitution performs a fixed local branch lookup without an injection path. A medium-risk workflow issue remains because the skill stages all changes and pushes without explicit approval.

remediation.issue: The workflow broadly stages, commits, and pushes repository changes without an explicit approval step.
remediation.suggestion: Inspect status and diffs, stage only intended files, and request user confirmation before every commit and push.

static_findings.snippet: The `bucket` field categorizes state into: `pass`, `fail`, `pending`, `skipping`, or `cancel`.
**Important:** If any of these checks are still `pending`, wait before proceeding:
- All CI checks are green (`bucket: pass`)
- Use `gh pr checks --required` to focus only on required checks
- Use `gh run view <run-id> --verbose` to see all job steps, not just failures
4. **Skip invalid feedback** - If the concern is not legitimate, move on

content.user_title: Resolve PR Failures Until CI Passes
content.value_statement: Pull request failures and scattered review feedback slow delivery. This skill investigates evidence, applies targeted fixes, and repeats checks until the branch is ready.
actual_capabilities: Identifies the pull request associated with the current branch.
Reads CI check states and waits for pending analysis checks.
Collects human reviews, inline comments, conversation comments, and bot feedback.
Inspects failed GitHub Actions logs before selecting a fix.
Applies targeted fixes, commits changes, pushes the branch, and waits for CI.
limitations: Requires an authenticated GitHub CLI installation.
Operates on the current branch and its associated pull request.
Can stage, commit, and push changes, so every diff requires review.
Cannot guarantee resolution of flaky, unrelated, or infrastructure failures.

use_cases.title: Repair a Failing Feature PR
use_cases.description: Trace failed checks, fix the responsible code, and monitor the next CI run.

use_cases.title: Process Review Feedback
use_cases.description: Collect human and automated comments, validate each concern, and address only confirmed issues.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Release Branch
use_cases.description: Verify required checks, investigate remaining failures, and report blockers before release approval.

prompt_templates.title: Check Pull Request Health
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the current pull request. Report failing or pending CI checks and summarize unresolved review feedback. Do not change files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a first inspection without repository changes.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Failed Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate failed CI logs for the current pull request. Explain each root cause, then propose the smallest targeted fixes before editing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when checks have failed and diagnosis is required.

prompt_templates.title: Address Valid Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Address valid CI failures and review comments. Show planned files, make targeted changes, run relevant tests, then request approval before committing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when diagnosis is complete and controlled changes are appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Controlled Iteration
prompt_templates.prompt: Iterate until required checks pass. Validate feedback, make minimal fixes, test, and pause before each commit or push. Stop after three repeated failures.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for advanced iteration with explicit approval gates.

output_examples.input: Check the current pull request and report its status without changing files.
output: Pull request 214 has two failed checks and one pending analysis check.
Type checking fails in the billing module, while an integration test times out.

output_examples.input: Investigate the failed checks and propose the smallest valid repair.
output: The type error comes from an outdated return annotation in the billing adapter.
The timeout is unrelated to this branch and has failed on the default branch.
Recommended action: update one annotation, run the focused test, and request approval before committing.

best_practices: Review failed logs and relevant source before modifying code.
Inspect repository status and diffs before staging any file.
Request explicit approval before each commit and remote push.
anti_patterns: Do not infer a root cause from a check name alone.
Do not stage unrelated changes with a broad repository command.
Do not repeat the same failed repair more than three times.

faq.question: What tools does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires Git, an authenticated GitHub CLI, and access to the pull request repository.

faq.question: Does it read review comments?
faq.answer: Yes. It gathers reviews, inline comments, conversation comments, and feedback from automated tools.

faq.question: Does it wait for pending checks?
faq.answer: Yes. It waits for pending analysis checks before acting, which reduces duplicate work.

faq.question: Can it change and push code?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflow can edit, stage, commit, and push repository changes.

faq.question: How does it handle invalid feedback?
faq.answer: It validates feedback against code and logs, then skips concerns that are not supported by evidence.

faq.question: When does the iteration stop?
faq.answer: It stops after success, a missing pull request, a required rebase, or three repeated failures needing user help.
